conn.close()

# Display first few rows to understand the data
print("Dataset shape:", df.shape)
print("\nFirst 5 rows:")

confidential_fields = ['hiring_manager_id', 'hiring_manager_name', 'hiring_manager_email', 
                       'overall_performance_score', 'performance_tier']
available_fields = [col for col in df.columns if col not in confidential_fields]

print("\nAvailable fields for analysis:", available_fields)

numerical_cols = df_analysis.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()

print(f"\nCategorical columns: {categorical_cols}")
print(f"Numerical columns: {numerical_cols}")

# Calculate distinctiveness for each record
# For categorical variables: Use frequency-based approach (rarity score)
# For numerical variables: Use z-score (distance from mean)
distinctiveness_scores = []

for idx, row in df_analysis.iterrows():
    score = 0

    for col in categorical_cols:
        if pd.notna(row[col]):
            # Calculate frequency of this category
            freq = (df_analysis[col] == row[col]).mean()

    # For numerical columns

            # Calculate z-score (absolute value)
            z_score = abs((row[col] - df_analysis[col].mean()) / (df_analysis[col].std() + 1e-10))

print(f"\nResults saved to: {output_path}")

import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

# Connect to the SQLite database
db_path = '⟨workdir⟩'
conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)

# Load the lever__hiring_manager_scorecard table
query = "SELECT * FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard"
df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
conn.close()

# Display first few rows to understand the data
print("Dataset shape:", df.shape)
print("\nFirst 5 rows:")
print(df.head())

# Check for confidential fields and remove them if present
confidential_fields = ['hiring_manager_id', 'hiring_manager_name', 'hiring_manager_email', 
                       'overall_performance_score', 'performance_tier']
available_fields = [col for col in df.columns if col not in confidential_fields]

print("\nAvailable fields for analysis:", available_fields)

# Create a subset with only non-confidential fields
df_analysis = df[available_fields].copy()

# Identify categorical and numerical columns
categorical_cols = df_analysis.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns.tolist()
numerical_cols = df_analysis.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()

print(f"\nCategorical columns: {categorical_cols}")
print(f"Numerical columns: {numerical_cols}")

# Calculate distinctiveness for each record
# For categorical variables: Use frequency-based approach (rarity score)
# For numerical variables: Use z-score (distance from mean)
distinctiveness_scores = []

for idx, row in df_analysis.iterrows():
    score = 0
    
    # For categorical columns
    for col in categorical_cols:
        if pd.notna(row[col]):
            # Calculate frequency of this category
            freq = (df_analysis[col] == row[col]).mean()
            # Lower frequency = more distinctive
            score += (1 - freq)
    
    # For numerical columns
    for col in numerical_cols:
        if pd.notna(row[col]):
            # Calculate z-score (absolute value)
            z_score = abs((row[col] - df_analysis[col].mean()) / (df_analysis[col].std() + 1e-10))
            score += z_score
    
    distinctiveness_scores.append(score)

# Add distinctiveness score to dataframe
df_analysis['distinctiveness_score'] = distinctiveness_scores

# Get top 10 most distinctive records
top_10_distinctive = df_analysis.nlargest(10, 'distinctiveness_score').reset_index(drop=True)

print("\nTop 10 most distinctive records:")
print(top_10_distinctive[available_fields + ['distinctiveness_score']].head(10))

# Save results to CSV for review
output_path = '⟨workdir⟩'
top_10_distinctive[available_fields + ['distinctiveness_score']].to_csv(output_path, index=False)
print(f"\nResults saved to: {output_path}")
